props.html:
With tile, the dirt is in the grout

Porcelain, travertine, limestone and glazed tile on alfresco areas, patios, balconies and pool surrounds. The tile face is usually close to non-porous, so almost nothing sticks to it. The grout between is porous, open and slightly recessed, which is where all of it goes.

  • Low pressure, the glaze sets the limit
  • Grout treated separately from the tile
  • Never acid on travertine or limestone
Get A Quote 0400 638 010
  1. Home
  2. Services
  3. Pressure and surface cleaning
  4. Outdoor tile cleaning

Two surfaces, one floor

A tiled outdoor area is really tile and grout, and they behave nothing like each other. Porcelain is vitrified and effectively non-porous, so dirt sits on it and comes off easily. Grout is cementitious, porous and sits a millimetre or two below the tile face, so it collects water, dirt and growth and holds all three.

Which is why a tiled patio that has been mopped still looks dirty. The tiles are clean and the grid of darker lines between them is not. Cleaning one is a rinse. Cleaning the other needs a solution, dwell time and usually a brush, and it is where the actual work on a tiled area goes.

By tile type

The glaze is what sets the pressure

The common outdoor tiles, and the thing that limits each one.
  Character How it is cleaned
Porcelain, unglazed or textured Vitrified, near zero porosity, usually a matt external grade Low pressure with a solution. Very forgiving, the grout is the job
Glazed ceramic A fired glass surface over a porous body Lowest pressure. The glaze micro-scratches and then holds dirt worse
Travertine Natural stone, porous, often with filled holes Low pressure, neutral chemistry. Acid dissolves it permanently
Limestone and marble Calcium based, softer than it looks Same as travertine. Never acid, test patch always
Slate and quartzite Layered, can flake along the bedding plane Low pressure only. Pressure lifts the layers
Terracotta and quarry tile Porous and usually sealed at some point in its life Gentle. The sealer condition decides what is possible

Swipe for the rest of the columns

The grout, properly

Where the work actually is

STEP 01

Treat, do not blast

Grout is cement. A high pressure jet erodes it out of the joint, which leaves a recess that collects more dirt than it did before and eventually lets water under the tile.

STEP 02

Solution and dwell

An alkaline cleaner left to work on the biological growth and the embedded soiling, which is most of what makes grout look dark.

STEP 03

Agitate the line

A brush along the joint rather than a nozzle at it. Slower, and it is the difference between grout that comes back and grout that looks slightly better.

STEP 04

Rinse and assess

Some grout is stained rather than dirty, usually where something was spilled. We will tell you which and whether colour sealing the grout is the honest answer.

Questions

Asked about outdoor tile

Can you pressure clean outdoor tiles?

At low pressure, yes. What is not safe is high pressure, which micro-scratches a glaze and erodes grout out of the joints. Both are permanent and both make the surface hold dirt worse afterwards.

On tile the chemistry does nearly all the work and the machine is mostly for rinsing.

My grout is still dark after cleaning. Why?

Because it is stained rather than dirty. Grout is porous, and oil, wine, rust and tannin go into it rather than onto it. Cleaning takes out everything that is on the surface, and what is left is in the material.

At that point the options are a grout colour seal, which recolours and seals the joint, or regrouting. Both are worth considering once rather than cleaning repeatedly and being disappointed.

Is acid safe on travertine?

No, never, and this is the single most important thing on this page. Travertine, limestone and marble are calcium based, and acid dissolves them. It leaves a dull etched patch that cannot be polished out or cleaned away.

A lot of general-purpose outdoor cleaners sold in hardware stores are acidic. If you have travertine, check before using anything on it.

Should outdoor tile be sealed?

The tile usually does not need it. Porcelain is already non-porous and a sealer sits on top doing very little. Travertine and limestone genuinely do benefit, because they are porous and stain easily.

Grout benefits almost always, on any tile type, because that is where the staining happens.

Can you clean a balcony without flooding the neighbours below?

Yes, and it needs planning rather than a hose. Water is controlled, drainage is checked before starting, and on an apartment balcony the method is closer to a wash and extract than a pressure clean.

Tell us it is a balcony when you book rather than when we arrive.
